step0_classification.evidence: one machine node (bare-metal machines / machine-agent) and one work queue each fan to 5 phase transitions (agent register+heartbeat, iPXE request, pull boot image, runs on host, run machine-audit / q enqueue, reinstall, audit, diagnose, diagnostic events), and the source marks every transition live ('add slow dots flowing through it'), so one dot per line.
tie_breakers_considered: Density: E=23 vs N=17, E clearly exceeds N, which pulls toward service-mesh/redundant-fabric.
Dots forbidden? No - the human asked for slow dots and then 'keep on dot alive per line', so it is not a fabric.

Phase order: the source narrates stages (request -> enqueue -> registry -> providers -> machines -> boot -> heartbeat) in one direction, which is the lifecycle-machines signature; the SKILL's own family table already names modal-machine-manager as a lifecycle-machines case.
Identifier/qualifier density is low (no addresses, no uncertainty markers), so identity-probe-maps does not apply.
secondary_recipes: service-mesh habit: the anti-parallel boot pair (mch->boot request, boot->mch response) is drawn in ONE view with two labels and two ports - no bidirectional arrow, no split across views.
identity-probe habit: every verb, payload and qualifier ('1 min', 'boot.ipxe + S3 args', 'verify reimage') is a ledger row with a named view before any spec existed.
